items.name: Cat-Cow
items.description: Slowly rounding and arching the spine on hands and knees to improve spinal mobility.
items.setup: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
steps: Breathe in and let your belly sink toward the floor while lifting your chest and gaze slightly (cow).
Breathe out and round your back toward the ceiling, tucking your chin and tailbone (cat).
Move slowly between the two positions.
Keep your arms straight and your weight evenly spread.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you arch and out as you round.
items.easier: Make the movement smaller, or do it seated with your hands on your knees.
cautions: Stay within a comfortable range for your back and neck.

items.name: Lunge with Rotation
items.description: A flowing lunge with a reach and twist that opens the hips, hamstrings and upper back.
items.setup: Start in a high plank. Step one foot forward outside the hand on the same side into a deep lunge, lowering the back knee to the floor if needed.
steps: Keep the opposite hand on the floor.
Rotate your chest toward the front leg and reach that arm toward the ceiling.
Bring the hand back down and gently shift your hips back to straighten the front leg.
Return to the lunge and repeat, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you rotate and reach, and in as you return.
items.easier: Keep the back knee on the floor and place your hand on a book or block.
items.harder: Hold each position for one slow breath.
cautions: Move within a comfortable range for your hips and back.

items.name: Side-Lying Open Book
items.description: Lying on your side and rotating your top arm open to improve upper-back rotation.
items.setup: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees and arms straight out in front of you, palms together. Rest your head on a cushion.
steps: Keep your knees together and on the floor.
Lift your top arm and sweep it over your body, rotating your chest toward the ceiling.
Let your head follow your hand and open the arm as far as is comfortable.
Bring the arm back to close the book. Repeat, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you open and in as you close.
mistakes: Forcing the arm down toward the floor.
items.easier: Rotate only part of the way.
items.harder: Pause for a full breath in the open position.
cautions: Keep the range comfortable for your shoulder.

items.name: Thread the Needle
items.description: A kneeling twist that slides one arm under the other to mobilise the upper back and shoulders.
items.setup: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
steps: Lift one hand and reach it toward the ceiling, rotating your chest open.
Sweep the arm down and slide it under the other arm, palm facing up.
Lower that shoulder and the side of your head gently toward the floor.
Pause, then return. Repeat, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you open up and out as you thread through.
mistakes: Shifting the hips to the side.
items.easier: Skip the upward reach and thread through only partway.
items.harder: Hold the threaded position for two slow breaths.
cautions: Avoid putting weight on your head or neck.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
items.description: Rotating both knees from side to side while seated to improve hip rotation.
items.setup: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet wider than hip-width. Place your hands behind you for support.
steps: Let both knees fall to one side so each knee forms roughly a right angle.
Sit tall as you settle into the position.
Lift the knees and rotate them over to the other side.
Move slowly and only as far as is comfortable. Each side counts as one repetition.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly, breathing out as the knees settle.
mistakes: Forcing the knees down to the floor.
items.easier: Keep your feet wider and lean back on your hands.
items.harder: Sit tall with your hands off the floor.
cautions: Stop if you feel pinching in the hips or pain in the knees.

items.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rock
items.description: Gently rocking the knee toward a wall to improve ankle bend, which helps with squats and lunges.
items.setup: Face a wall in a staggered stance or half-kneeling position with your front foot a few centimetres from the wall. Rest your hands on the wall.
steps: Keep your front heel on the floor.
Rock your front knee forward toward the wall, in line with your second toe.
Pause briefly, then rock back.
Repeat, then switch legs.
mistakes: Bouncing in and out of the position.
items.easier: Move your foot closer to the wall.
items.harder: Move your foot slightly further from the wall.
cautions: You should feel a stretch in the calf or ankle, never a sharp pain.

items.name: Wall Angel
items.description: Sliding the arms up and down a wall to mobilise the shoulders and wake up the upper back.
items.setup: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet a short step away from it. Place your arms against the wall with elbows bent at 90 degrees, like a goalpost.
steps: Keep your lower back gently in contact with the wall and your ribs down.
Slide your arms up the wall as far as you can while keeping contact.
Slide them back down to the goalpost position.
Move slowly and smoothly.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you slide up and in as you slide down.
mistakes: Arching the lower back away from the wall.
Forcing the hands to stay on the wall when your range is limited.
items.easier: Step your feet further from the wall and reduce the range.
items.harder: Hold the top position for two seconds.
cautions: Work within a comfortable shoulder range.

items.name: Supported Deep Squat Hold
items.description: Resting in a deep squat while holding onto support to improve hip and ankle mobility.
items.setup: Stand facing a door frame or a sturdy piece of furniture, feet a little wider than shoulder-width and toes turned out. Hold the support with both hands.
steps: Lower slowly into a deep squat, using the support to control the descent.
Let your hips sink between your heels and keep your chest lifted.
Relax into the position while keeping your knees in line with your toes.
Hold and breathe, then use the support to stand up.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly and deeply as you relax into the position.
mistakes: Letting the heels lift (place a folded towel under them if needed).
items.easier: Squat only partway, or sit on a low stool.
cautions: Avoid this exercise if deep knee bending is painful.
Stand up slowly to avoid feeling dizzy.
